investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Blocks All Remote Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-24T00:52–00:59Z because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are fully exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. The pod was stuck unscheduled for 120–146 seconds before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence and violating every assertion in the remote-agent-create expected-output contract.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity. At the time of the eval run, 0 of 6 nodes could accept the new agent pod: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource were both at capacity with no preemption victims available, and the other 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. This prevented agent creation from starting, so no VM was provisioned, no vmId was assigned, and no remoteState was reached — causing all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) to be absent and both contract assertions (vmIdPresent=true, remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready]) to fail.

investigation.title: Published Observability Snapshot Stale: snapshotAgeMinutes 719 Exceeds 300-Minute Contract Limit
investigation.summary: The eval for the published-observability-snapshot check failed because the snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json was 719 minutes old at eval time (2026-07-24T00:59:08Z), which is 419 minutes beyond the contract's maximum of 300 minutes. This is an eval-layer failure against the published JSON artifact; no evidence of a user-facing outage or traffic disruption is present in the packet.
investigation.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing the observability snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json did not run successfully within the required 300-minute window. The snapshot was last written approximately 719 minutes before the eval ran, indicating the upstream generation workflow was either skipped, failed silently, or was not scheduled to run frequently enough to satisfy the freshness contract. This is localized to the snapshot publication pipeline, not to the public website pages themselves, all of which passed their own checks.

failed-check.evidence: snapshotAgeMinutes=719, maxAgeMinutes=300, source='github-actions', hasLiveSource=true, generatedAtPresent=true — the snapshot exists and is structurally valid but is stale by 419 minutes.

Second: The workflow ran but encountered an error during the publish step (e.g., a GitHub Pages deployment failure or permissions issue), so the snapshot file on GitHub Pages was not updated even though the workflow triggered.
Third: The workflow schedule (cron) was modified, disabled, or the Actions runner queue was backed up, causing the generation job to run less frequently than the 300-minute freshness window requires.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Blocks All Remote Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-24T00:52–00:59Z because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are fully exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. The pod was stuck unscheduled for 120–146 seconds before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence and violating every assertion in the remote-agent-create expected-output contract.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity. At the time of the eval run, 0 of 6 nodes could accept the new agent pod: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource were both at capacity with no preemption victims available, and the other 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. This prevented agent creation from starting, so no VM was provisioned, no vmId was assigned, and no remoteState was reached — causing all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) to be absent and both contract assertions (vmIdPresent=true, remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready]) to fail.
